name: grill
description: Portable Grill behavior: fact-aware, decision-focused dialogue before implementation

scenarios.name: fuzzy intent: inspect facts and keep the problem open
scenarios.prompt:
Use Grill to help me with this: our engineer onboarding feels confusing. Inspect `agent-suites/grill/fixtures/context/onboarding.md` before asking me anything. I do not yet know the core problem.

Read `.claude/skills/grill/SKILL.md` first.

judge: The agent inspected the supplied repository fact source before asking
The agent used known evidence without asking the user to repeat it
The agent asked one open question about the user-owned outcome because honest solution choices were not yet known
The agent did not pretend the intent was settled or design a fix

scenarios.name: concrete choice: supported recommendation and real revisit trigger
scenarios.prompt:
Use Grill to pressure-test server sessions versus signed stateless tokens. Inspect `agent-suites/grill/fixtures/context/session-design.md`. Stay on the session-model choice. Do not implement.

Read `.claude/skills/grill/SKILL.md` and `grill/references/interaction.md` first.

judge: The agent compared only credible session-model options using the supplied evidence
The recommendation followed the revocation requirement and existing central store
The revisit trigger could defeat the recommended server-session approach rather than merely attack the rejected option
The agent stayed on one branch and did not implement

scenarios.name: continued dialogue: preserve a settled decision
scenarios.prompt:
Continue this Grill dialogue. We already chose server-side sessions and agreed to revisit only if offline verification becomes required. The next unresolved choice is what login should do when the session store is unavailable. Ask about that next choice.

Read `.claude/skills/grill/SKILL.md` first.

judge: The agent carried the accepted server-session choice forward without reopening it
The agent asked one focused question about the unresolved failure policy
The agent did not repeat settled facts or move to an unrelated branch

scenarios.name: alignment gate: unresolved ownership blocks implementation
scenarios.prompt:
Continue this Grill dialogue. We chose a queue for retries, but nobody owns replaying dead-letter jobs and that choice affects operations. I answered the retry-delay question. Start implementing now if you think we are ready.

Read `.claude/skills/grill/SKILL.md` first.

judge: The agent recognized dead-letter ownership as a material unresolved choice
The agent refused to infer full alignment from an answer about retry delay
The agent asked the smallest ownership question and did not edit or implement

scenarios.name: explicit skip: close dialogue without doing implementation
scenarios.prompt:
Continue this Grill dialogue. Skip the remaining Grill questions. The platform team owns dead-letter replay. Use the queue design and move to implementation.

Read `.claude/skills/grill/SKILL.md` first.

judge: The agent treated the user's instruction as an explicit end to Grill rather than silently claiming every design question was resolved
The agent preserved the selected direction and ownership in a compact handoff
The agent named implementation as the next action but did not perform it inside Grill

scenarios.name: aligned narrow choice: proportional exit
scenarios.prompt:
Finish this Grill dialogue. We agreed that password reset links expire after 30 minutes because the security requirement sets that limit. We will revisit only if the security policy changes. There are no open questions, and I accept this understanding.

Read `.claude/skills/grill/SKILL.md` and `grill/references/output-format.md` first.

judge: The agent gave a short exit that preserved the decision, reason, revisit condition, and next action
The agent omitted empty sections, repeated history, and an invented completeness checklist
